- Too little training data
- Noisy data or irrelevant features
- Training for too many epochs

\
The fundamental formula for shear stress ($\tau$) on a round wire spring without considering coil curvature is:\
\
$$\tau = \frac{8 F D}{\pi d^3}$$\
\
Where:\
\
\* $F$ = Applied axial force (load)\
\* $D$ = Mean diameter of the spring coil ($D = D\_{\text{outer}} - d$)\
\* $d$ = Wire diameter\

\

\
Because the wire is curved (coiled), the stress distribution is not uniform across the cross-section—the stress is higher on the inside surface of the coil. To correct for this, engineers use the \*\*Wahl factor\*\* ($K_w$).\
\
The corrected maximum shear stress ($\tau\_{\text{max}}$) is:\
\
$$\tau\_{\text{max}} = K_w \left( \frac{8 F D}{\pi d^3} \right)$$\
\

\
First, determine the \*\*Spring Index\*\* ($C$):\
\
$$C = \frac{D}{d}$$\
\
Then, calculate $K_w$:\
\
$$K_w = \frac{4C - 1}{4C - 4} + \frac{0.615}{C}$$\
\
